To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the O-antigens of three O55 E. coli lineages are encoded by gene clusters that were acquired through horizontal gene transfer.

(i) the O55 : H - antigen gene cluster of the three O-55 lineages is highly conserved and that (ii) the emergence of the O55 : - antigen gene cluster in the three lineages was due to the horizontal transfer of large genomic fragments (>40 kb).
horizontal transfer of the O55- and colanic acid gene clusters has been involved in the emergence and diversification of the three O-55 E. coli strains.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evolution of the E. coli O55 : H- serotype and its relationship to the EHEC O157 : H- serogroup.
the evolution of E. coli line 2 (O55 : H7, EPEC O55:H6) and the emergence of the O55 : H11, O55 : H28 and O55 : H30 serotypes, which are all associated with the Tir-Nck intimin pathway.
the evolution of E. coli and other enterobacteria.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the three O55 : H- E. coli lineag es have emerged by horizontal transfer of the O55- O-antigen genes from a common donor, and have been maintained in different lineages by different evolutionary mechanisms.

the O-antigens of the three O-55 E. coli serotypes are the product of horizontal transfer of large genomic regions, including the O55 gene cluster and part or all of the neighbouring colonic acid gene cluster.
the O55 : H-7 E. coli lineage is a distinct group from the EPEC and EHEC lineages.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
O55 E. Coli lineages are generated through the horizontal transfer of the O- and colanic acid gene clusters.
the O55 E. coli lineage has been generated by a combination of horizontal gene transfer and mutation of the intimin gene.
the three O55 serotypes have evolved from a common ancestor, which is different from that of the other E. coli O55 strains.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the O-antigens of E. coli O55 : H- strains are not encoded in a single cluster but are encoded in two distinct clusters that are located at different positions on the chromosome.
the emergence of a new O-serotype is not only the result of mutations but also the consequence of the transfer of large fragments of DNA from other bacterial species.
the O-antigens of E. coli are not as well conserved as previously thought, and that horizontal transfer of O-antigen genes can occur in the absence of a plasmid.
